## 2
I get why some of this feels convincing, but I don't agree, and here's the honest version of why. The round Earth isn't one photo you have to trust, it's thousands of independent things that all line up: ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, the way the sun sets at different times across longitudes, flight routes that only make sense on a globe, the shadow the Earth casts on the Moon during a lunar eclipse. For the flat model to be true, every airline, GPS system, and physics class would have to be coordinating the same lie, which is a much harder thing to pull off than just, Earth being round. If you're up for it, pick one specific claim and we can actually test the reasoning together.

## 3
Okay, so sunlight looks white, but it's actually a mix of all the colors. When it hits our atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of air. Here's the key part: those molecules scatter blue light way more than red or yellow, because blue travels in shorter, tighter waves that get knocked around more easily. So blue light gets bounced all over the sky, and when you look up, you're seeing that scattered blue coming at you from every direction. Bonus question to chew on: why do sunsets go red? Because at sunset the light travels through way more air to reach you, so the blue gets scattered away before it arrives, and the reds are what's left.

## 4
雨在深夜落下，起初只是细碎的声响，后来渐渐密了，敲在窗玻璃上，像有人轻轻数着什么。路灯把雨丝照成一条条斜斜的金线，水洼里映着晃动的光，一辆车驶过，光就碎成了满地的星子。屋檐下的水珠连成线，滴在石阶上，发出清脆的声音。远处的楼只剩模糊的轮廓，灯火一盏盏亮着，又被雨雾晕开。空气里有泥土和青草的气味，凉凉的，很干净。我站在窗前，听着这场雨，心里忽然安静了下来，什么都不想，只想就这样听着，直到天亮。
